text:
Maya R.: Quick heads-up — noticed erasure queue backpressure for EU DSAR deletes hitting the keystore path this morning, looks like some RBAC deny errors spiking. Anyone oncall?
Samir Patel: on it, grabbing logs now. Which keystore? EU KMS or our staging keystore?
Maya R.: EU KMS (redwood-eu-keystore). Error pattern: `403: access denied` from `keystore-service` when service acct tries to call `Decrypt` during delete verification.
Elsa Nguyen: that sounds like the service-account role change we rolled last week. I flagged a possible regression in the RBAC mapping table.
Kevin Cho: pinging infra to check recent terraform rolls. If the SA lost `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` we will see that.
Samir Patel: pasting a sample log: `2024-10-14T09:12:23Z keystore-service ERROR req=0xabc decryption_failed user=svc-dsar-worker reason=permission_denied key=projects/redwood-eu/locations/global/keyRings/erasure/cryptoKeys/erasure-key`
Elsa Nguyen: ok, two immediate asks: 1) temporary allow so in-flight erasures finish, 2) ensure audit logging captures the allow/deny and any manual overrides for DSAR evidence.
Maya R.: +1. We need the audit record because legal asked for a retention-exception timeline last month and we can't have blind holes. @Sara L (Legal) FYI — potential short delay in completing some erasures.
Sara L (Legal): thanks for the ping. If there's a retention exception window needed we need explicit timestamps in the audit trail. Please log who approved any temporary perms.
Kevin Cho: I can open an emergency change: grant `roles/cloudkms.viewer` & `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `svc-dsar-worker@redwood-prod` for 30 minutes, and we’ll rotate after. Need two approvals in chat.
Samir Patel: I approve.
Elsa Nguyen: I approve, but request we capture the change in `ops-audit` and tag it `dsar-emergency-rbac` so it's queryable.
audit-bot: CHG-9831 applied by Kevin Cho at 09:20Z — temporary roles attached to svc-dsar-worker for 30m. Audit export scheduled to s3://redwood-audit/exports/2024-10-14/dsar-emergency-rbac.json
Maya R.: thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) can we get a short-term mitigation to backpressure the erasure queue to avoid request retries until the fix rolls? 2) long-term: how do we avoid RBAC drift between staging and prod Keystore policies?
Kevin Cho: added a `delete-throttle` flag to the erasure-worker config so we can pause new deletes while letting retries finish: `ERASURE_DELETE_THROTTLE=250ms` (default 50ms). Rolling this to EU region now.
Samir Patel: rolled. Observability: saw retry 429s drop by ~60% in the last 3 mins.
Elsa Nguyen: for long-term, proposal: nightly reconciliation job that diff's keystore IAM bindings vs canonical policy in git, create PRs for drift and alert if a key loses required bindings. Also add an integration test in the release pipeline that validates `svc-dsar-worker` has `decrypt` permission on targeted keys.
Maya R.: sounds good. Make an engineering ticket and tag `security` + `legal` so we can track compliance requirements.
Kevin Cho: created ticket INFRA-1248 with checklist: ``
- nightly iam-diff job
- pipeline integration test
- audit-export retention 90d
- alerting on binding removals
``
Samir Patel: one more thing — vulnerability triage note: the recent KMS client CVE we patched last month might have changed client behavior around retries; we should verify no edge-case where retries cause duplicate deletes before decryption verification completes.
Elsa Nguyen: good catch. I'll add a test in the vuln-triage doc to simulate `Decrypt` 403 + transient 500 to verify idempotency.
Sara L (Legal): keep me posted. If any records fall into retention-exception category we need evidence: who requested the exception, reason, and approval chain.
Maya R.: copying summary for the DSAR log: `time_window=2024-10-14T09:12:23Z-09:40Z action=erasure pause reason=rbac_deny mitigation=temporary_role_attach approvers=[Samir,Elsa] audit_export=s3://redwood-audit/exports/2024-10-14/dsar-emergency-rbac.json`
Samir Patel: closing the loop — the keystore policy drift was the cause, reverted unintended change in terraform state, and we scheduled the nightly iam-diff. No evidence of missed deletes after the temporary window.
Maya R.: thanks all. Filing for retention-exception review (no exception needed now) and following up on INFRA-1248. :thumbsup:
Kevin Cho: also added a quickrun doc in `eng-security` about emergency keystore RBAC recovery steps. Link: https://confluence/redwood/secure/keystore-rbac-recovery
Elsa Nguyen: and added the integration test PR to the release branch.
Sara L (Legal): acked. Document the approvals in case of audits.
Maya R.: great. closing thread.
